tools.name: Stable Diffusion
tools.desc: Open-source AI model for text-to-image generation
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Stable Diffusion homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.

tools.name: CompVis Diffusion Models
tools.desc: Collection of diffusion models for image generation
pros: Free and open source, transparent code, self-hostable for full data control
Supports local / Docker deployment, better data privacy
Free version available, zero cost for personal use
cons: Requires some technical skill to deploy and configure
usage:
Step: Check your environment
This tool runs locally. First make sure your computer meets the basics.
Tip:
Install the required runtime (see README).
Check:
Open a terminal and type `the command`. If you see a version number, your environment is OK.

Step: Download the code to your machine
Open a terminal in a folder you like and run the commands below:
Code:
git clone https://github.com/CompVis/stable-diffusion.git
cd stable-diffusion
Tip:
New to git? If it says command not found, download it from https://git-scm.com.

Step: Install dependencies
The project needs some extra building blocks to run.
Code:
make install
Tip:
If a command errors, it is usually a network issue. Python users can try a mirror.

Step: Fill in the API Key / account config
Many AI tools need a model connection. Find the config item in the README and fill it in.
Code:
# Example: replace xxx with your real Key
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-xxx"
Tip:
Do not screenshot your Key in public groups. Get a free/cheap Key (e.g. GLM-4, DeepSeek) to practice.

Step: Start and run your first task
Run the example command from the project and watch the terminal output.
Code:
./run.sh
Check:
If the program prints results (no red Error text), you have it working.

Step: Troubleshooting
Failing the first local deploy is normal. Common issues:
1. Dependency version mismatch → use the Python/Node version the repo recommends;
2. Key not working → check your environment variables;
3. Cannot reach the model API → switch mirror or provider.
Tip:
See more examples in "Related tutorials" below, or click "Visit official site".
